activity_context.topic_title: Defining Definite Integrals Using Left and Right Riemann Sums

feedback.problem:
Find the function $f(x)$ and the value of $b,$ given that

$$
{\int }_{2}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}[({2}^{\,2+3k/n}+1)\cdot \frac{3}{n}].
$$

$\,f(x)=$
{{field-1}} $\,$ and 
$\,b=$
{{field-2}}
feedback.worked_solution:
A definite integral can be defined as the limit of a left Riemann sum as follows:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx
$$

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{k}=a+kΔx.$

Notice that we're given that the lower limit $a=2.$ 

Comparing the given summation with the general expression above, we see that $Δx=\frac{3}{n}.$ Therefore, 

$$
\frac{3}{n}=\frac{b-2}{n}\,⟹\,b=5.
$$

Consequently, ${x}_{k}=2+\frac{3k}{n}$ and $f({x}_{k})={2}^{\,{x}_{k}}+1.$

Hence,

$$
{\int }_{2}^{5}({2}^{x}+1)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=0}^{n-1}[({2}^{\,2+3k/n}+1)\cdot \frac{3}{n}].
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is 

$$
f(x)={2}^{x}+1\,\text{and}\,b=5.
$$
